gloss: front and back; two sides; duplicity

definitions.explanation: The two physical surfaces of something — the front side and the reverse side.
The idea that something has two contrasting aspects. Used to describe situations where opposing qualities coexist.
Having a hidden side that contradicts one's outward appearance. Used to describe inconsistency between words and actions, or public and private behavior.

notes:
Read as ひょうり in this compound form. The same kanji can be read as おもてうら in the native Japanese reading.

The key compound ⟦{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}→表裏一体：14082_hyouriittai⟧ ('two sides forming one body') is an important four-character idiom meaning that two contrasting things are inseparably connected.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{表裏一体|ひょうりいったい}→表裏一体：14082_hyouriittai⟧ (two sides of the same coin)
- {表裏|ひょうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a two-faced person)
- {表裏|ひょうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a straightforward person)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表裏|ひょうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧ (a relationship of two sides)
- {表裏|ひょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}い{分|わ}ける→使い分ける：07666_tsukaiwakeru⟧ (to use different faces in different situations)
